question: Should ClawScan adopt the canonical Codex reviewer execution boundary, model fallback, and supported-engine contract exactly as synchronized from openclaw/agent-skills?
rationale: The implementation is internally consistent and well tested, but it deliberately changes how a security-sensitive reviewer can inspect code and the web, as well as existing automation defaults; source review cannot authorize that policy choice.

options.title: Adopt Canonical Boundary
options.body: Accept the canonical model, constrained inspection tools, optional web search, fallback, and engine fail-closed behavior as ClawScan's autoreview contract.

options.title: Revise Upstream First
options.body: Pause this synchronization and change the canonical openclaw/agent-skills implementation first if ClawScan cannot accept the new boundary.

recommendation.title: Adopt Canonical Boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the canonical model, constrained inspection tools, optional web search, fallback, and engine fail-closed behavior as ClawScan's autoreview contract.
